articles.title: Functions in CSS?
articles.description: We can’t use custom CSS functions in production just yet, but this early look at how they’re currently being prototyped in Chrome Canary offers a glimpse at the future capabilities (arguments, type-checking, etc).
articles.author: Juan Diego Rodríguez

articles.title: Views on 'Views'
articles.description: Discussions are underway to potentially change the definition of a ‘web page’ to best accommodate the various contexts in which we can now interact with web content (such as in native apps or VR). One such suggestion is to use ‘view’.
articles.author: Hidde de Vries

articles.title: ▶  Everything You Need to Know About Invoker Commands
articles.description: command and commandfor attributes are a brand new HTML web platform feature coming later in 2025. Here’s everything you need to know about them, plus some things you really don’t.
articles.author: Keith Cirkel

articles.title: Truth, Lies and Progress Bars
articles.description: Yeah, sometimes loading/progress indicators lie because demonstrating some amount of forward momentum gives users oft-needed confidence that things are continuing as intended. There’s a few things we can do to enhance that experience — as Tyler touches on here.
articles.author: Tyler Sticka

articles.title: Trusting AI with My Images Wasn't Easy
articles.description: We shared last week how Dries was experimenting with various LLMs for writing alt-text for thousands of images. Here he reflects on the effort, concluding that “sometimes, the best way to improve is to step aside and let a tool do the job better”
articles.author: Dries Buytaert

articles.title: CSS Meets Voxel Art: Building a Rendering Engine with Stacked Grids
articles.description: Another great tutorial from Codrops, this time showing how transforms, perspective, and stacked grids can create a fully addressable 3D space, pushing the boundaries of just what’s possible with pure CSS. You can create your own voxel creations here.
articles.author: Agustin Capeletto

articles.title: ⭐️ Building a CSS-Only Star Rating Component
articles.description: A tutorial you’ve no doubt seen countless times, but typically relying on a little bit of JavaScript. Temani shares a strictly CSS-only approach.
articles.author: Temani Afif

articles.title: Fixing rowspan=0 on Tables on WebKit
articles.description: Curious as to how a browser bug gets fixed? This post is a detailed walkthrough of that process.
articles.author: Karl Dubost

articles.title: A Chrome on Android Edge-to-Edge Migration Guide
articles.description: Bramus shares an update regarding edge-to-edge display support in Android, and how to migrate your site to support this feature – especially if you’re using position: fixed content at bottom: 0.
articles.author: Bramus Van Damme (Google)

articles.title: Building Websites with 'LLMs'
articles.description: That’s (L)ots of (L)ittle ht(M)l page(S) by the way. 😜 Jim shares an approach for building pages with less reliance on JavaScript-injected content.
articles.author: Jim Nielsen

articles.title: The Case for Minimal WordPress Setups: A Contrarian View on Theme Frameworks
articles.description: Kevin thinks modern frameworks “cause far more problems than they solve” — as such, he asks why they’re so popular, and whether they really benefit developers in the long run?
articles.author: Kevin Leary

articles.title: Astro 5.4: A Picture-Perfect Release
articles.description: The popular content site framework introduces several key improvements, including remote image optimization in Markdown, experimental responsive image support in Markdown, new configuration helpers and more.
articles.author: Matt Kane

articles.title: Kibo UI: A Registry of Accessible Components Designed to Use with shadcn/ui
articles.description: A modest set of about 20+ components that use the shadcn/ui CSS variables and they work well as building blocks for more complex components.
articles.author: Hayden Bleasel

articles.title: Stylelint: A 'Mighty' Modern Style Linter
articles.description: An established linter with over 100 built-in rules to help “catch errors, apply limits and enforce stylistic conventions”. GitHub repo.
articles.author: stylelint

articles.title: Freesound: A Collaborative Collection of 670,000+ Free Sounds
articles.description: Downloadable in WAV format, possibly useful for adding UI sounds to an app, or for adding to videos. Take note of the license for any sound, as not all are CC.
articles.author: Universitat Pompeu Fabra

articles.title: Pierre: A Striking New Web Site with a Git Platform Attached
articles.description: Pierre bills itself as a ‘new Git platform’ but everyone on social media this week was more wowed by its far out Web design rather than what it’s selling. It evokes early 00s Web experiences with a blend of modern Web technology and retro glitchy aesthetic. One to be seen.
articles.author: Pierre Computer Company
